figmaExecutionNotes: Use Plus Jakarta Sans for headlines and Inter for body text as the default Techjockey category pairing.
Keep the hero background dark and use the left column for a compact creative form; do not make the hero centered.
Prioritize logo trust above any stat-based trust treatment because the brief explicitly says visitors trust logos most.
Use consistent white card surfaces with 1px borders and 12px radius for feature cards and 8px radius or stronger elevation for pricing/testimonial cards.
Do not invent unsupported sections such as news or why-Techjockey; they are excluded because content is not supplied or explicitly disabled.
Use section spacing from the design memory: 96px desktop and 64px mobile, with tighter card internal spacing for dense product content.
Seedream and Seedance should share a common product-section template while remaining clearly distinct through section labels and copy hierarchy.
Treat pricing as a quote-led conversion section rather than a checkout module; keep the CTA text exactly as provided.

heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 (Image Generation) and Seedance 1.5 Pro (Video Generation) - advanced foundation models developed by ByteDance for high-quality visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected editorial split: place the content column on the right and a large layered studio mockup on the left. The hero visual should feel premium and tangible, combining image outputs, video frames, prompt UI, and subtle waveform cues in a single composited JPEG. Keep the orange brand hero with black/white contrast, add a soft noise texture plus mesh gradient for depth, and use floating SVG chips to reinforce the two products. CTA buttons must be solid orange. Avoid neon/futuristic styling; this should feel like a high-end B2B magazine spread with enterprise polish and strong conversion intent.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a split-screen hero, then immediately switch to a high-contrast marquee trust bar to avoid repeating the same visual density.
Use an alternating product rhythm: Seedream as a spotlight-plus-grid editorial block, Seedance as a darker split-panel or accordion-style block with a different reading pace.
Insert a compact credibility section before pricing so the page doesn’t feel like a linear feature dump.
Make testimonials a carousel to compress proof and break the card-grid cadence.
Use a floating lead-form card near the end to change from reading mode to action mode.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image & Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Seedream 4.5 for high-fidelity AI image generation and Seedance 1.5 Pro for cinematic AI video creation with audio, multilingual lip-sync, and enterprise-grade creative control.

sections.designNote: Make the hero content-first but highly dynamic: left side carries the long headline, tight supporting copy, and a compact CTA stack; right side shows a premium studio-style composite with image outputs, video frames, prompt chips, and small floating product tags for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Keep the composition polished and conversion-focused rather than futuristic.

Place trust immediately after the hero as a dense, dark marquee band. Since social proof inputs are sparse, use an enterprise credibility strip with logo placeholders, capability claims, and short proof phrases. This should feel prominent and fast-moving, creating strong contrast after the orange hero.

Use two distinct product blocks with alternating visual rhythm. Lead with Seedream 4.5 in a spotlight-plus-grid layout: one large feature story panel on the left and a clean feature grid on the right. Then switch style for Seedance 1.5 Pro into a darker or reversed split-panel presentation with stronger motion cues and an accordion-like feature list. Because both products have 5 features, avoid simple flat grids throughout; instead use a spotlight first, then a different reading pattern for the second block.

Keep this section compact and utility-oriented, even though include=false means it can be minimized or omitted in implementation. If retained, frame it as a brief reassurance block with 3-4 cards covering evaluation support, quick demo access, and enterprise buying confidence. Visually, it should feel lighter and quieter than the product sections.

Use a centered pricing card composition with one highlighted card for Seedance 1.5 Pro and a secondary card for Seedream 4.5. Keep this section editorial rather than transactional: price and quote actions should be clear, but not overly aggressive. Add a thin trust strip or subtle proof line near the pricing cards to reduce friction.

Convert the five testimonials into a dark, premium carousel to break the white-card rhythm and compress a lot of proof into a high-impact, story-like band. Prioritize roles like Creative Director, Video Producer, Art Director, and Marketing Manager. Use large quote marks and minimal chrome.

Finish with a floating, high-intent lead form card that feels like the conversion endpoint of the page. Because the hero already carried the main CTA, this form should be calmer and more consultative than aggressive. Place it against a soft neutral background with strong visual separation from the testimonial carousel.

Use this only if additional media or brand logos exist; otherwise omit. If included, make it a restrained horizontal logo strip or utility footer-like band so the page ends cleanly without adding more conversion pressure.

blueprint.designPersonality: Premium editorial B2B with strong enterprise proof, clean contrast, and a creative studio feel. It should feel intelligent, composed, and conversion-focused rather than futuristic or neon. The layout should feel like a high-end product magazine meets software marketplace: bold orange hero, white content panels, black trust bands, floating chips, and carefully structured sections for image generation, video generation, and pricing.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a large, polished JPEG hero visual showing AI-generated creative work in a layered studio-like mockup: one side with image generation outputs and the other with cinematic video frames, audio waveform hints, and prompt controls. Add floating badges for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro, plus a visible enterprise logo proof band. Support sections can use PNG UI shells and SVG icons; logos must be SVG. Since trust is key, include a dense logo marquee directly under the hero and a secondary trust strip near pricing.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and needs to fit a premium split hero with form and visual area, so a smaller hero size keeps balance and prevents awkward wrapping.

colours.colourReason: The brand palette is derived exclusively from the supplied Techjockey colors: orange, white, black, and soft grey. Orange is used as the primary hero background and CTA color, while black and white create premium editorial contrast. No extra palette colors are introduced.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen split hero with brand/logo placement, large bold headline, short supporting copy, and a compact bullet/value list; primary conversion CTA is surfaced near the hero content with strong visual hierarchy.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Top-heavy landing page flow: hero first, then a lead capture/form block, followed by modular product/feature sections; content is grouped into stacked sections with clear heading hierarchy and minimal visual interruption.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Functional form and content cards with simple rectangular structure, subtle framing, and utility-first layout; no evidence of decorative glassmorphism or heavy shadow treatment in the reference HTML.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA-led conversion flow with one dominant action in the hero and a secondary CTA pattern in product sections when needed; CTAs are likely prominent, rectangular, and placed near persuasive copy rather than repeated excessively.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module is present in the reference structure, so pricing behavior should default to omitted or collapsed into a later conversion section if needed.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not represented in the provided HTML; default to a minimal utility footer or omit if the page is kept as a focused lead-gen landing page.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the hero aside from logo and icon bullets; product-heavy pages should use optional supporting imagery or diagrams only if they reinforce comprehension, not as a dominant carousel/media strip.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Modular feature sections with a clear product label, headline, descriptive paragraph, CTA, and a feature list; best treated as stacked content blocks with strong information hierarchy and progressive disclosure of details.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form block near the top of the page, visually separated from the hero and optimized for conversion; hidden metadata fields indicate a form-driven acquisition pattern with utility styling and straightforward field layout.
referenceMap.animationStyle: If motion is used, it should be lightweight and utility-driven, aligned to carousel/slide behavior rather than elaborate reveal animations.
designNotes: Optimize for conversion and clarity over storytelling complexity.
Use a strong first-screen headline, concise benefit bullets, and a clear CTA.
Keep section structure modular so multiple product lines can be repeated consistently.
Prefer simple layout hierarchy, compact form placement, and low-distraction surfaces.
If adding richer media, keep it secondary to the message and CTA.

blueprint.additionalInstructions:
PROOF STRATEGY: The visitor trusts logos most. Make this the dominant trust signal.

Add form on left side of the hero banner make it creative

mustHaveMoments: Left-side hero lead form with a creative, high-contrast treatment
Prominent logo-trust strip above or near the hero form
Clear split between Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro with distinct value propositions
Outcome-focused feature blocks emphasizing quality, speed, fidelity, and multimodal capability
Testimonials from relevant creative roles to reinforce credibility
Pricing/quote section positioned after product proof, not too early
avoidPatterns: Generic abstract AI visuals without product relevance
Badge-heavy trust styling that dilutes the logo-first strategy
Overly decorative layouts, glassmorphism, or heavy shadow effects
Long unbroken text walls in the hero
Multiple competing CTAs above the fold
Overly dense sections that reduce scanability
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is a high-intent lead-generation landing page for a solution-aware audience evaluating advanced AI image and video models. The strongest conversion path is a product-led narrative supported by logo-first trust, because the brief explicitly says visitors trust logos most. The hero should use a split layout with a creative left-side form to capture leads immediately while the right side communicates the product promise and visual credibility. Since the page is category-oriented but goal-focused on a single conversion outcome, the design should prioritize immediate form engagement, concise proof, and clear product differentiation. The tone should feel confident and premium rather than playful, with balanced density so technical buyers can scan features, testimonials, and pricing without feeling overwhelmed.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
